lead.cert: A Let's Encrypt wildcard certificate for all ticked myaddr names (Names page, column Certificate), delivered to the reverse proxy.
lead.log: The latest messages of the agent.

lead.push: Messages on VPN switches, outages and errors.
lead.rewrite: Fixed entry addresses redirect to the current target with the VPN port.

myaddr.ddns_a_eintrag_automatisch_aktual: DDNS: update the A record automatically
myaddr.die_offentliche_ip_deines_anschlu: The public IP of your home line is never reported.
myaddr.dort_name_reservieren_den_schluss: (reserve a name there and copy the key once). portnook sets the A record to the VPN exit IP and renews it at least every 30 days, otherwise myaddr deletes the record. All subnames (e.g. app.<name>.myaddr.tools) point to the same IP.
myaddr.ist_das_vpn_aus_oder: If the VPN is off or the exit IP unknown, the fallback IP is reported. Without a fallback IP there is no update and the old record stays.
myaddr.namen_liste_hint: All names are equal, the column Use says what a name is for. Connection: points to the VPN exit IP; with one or more VPN profiles to the exit IP of a running tunnel of these profiles (active or standby), and the redirect uses it while it serves the active tunnel. Several names may share profiles; the active tunnel and the standby never get the same name, the active tunnel first. A name without a free tunnel keeps its record; without a profile to the exit IP of the active profile. Entry/rewrite: fixed name of the redirect host, points to its fixed IP (public or internal). Column Certificate: the name goes into the shared certificate with *.. The first connection name without a profile is the base name: it is always in the certificate, the settings below the table apply to it, and the redirect falls back to it. When a name changes its use, its key is kept.
myaddr.hauptname_einstellungen: Settings for names without a VPN profile
myaddr.weitere_namen_hint: Entry/rewrite: fixed name of the redirect host, points to its fixed IP (public or internal). Connection/endpoint: like the main name points to the VPN exit IP and follows every switch at once. With a VPN profile the name always points to the exit IP of that profile (also as standby), and the redirect uses it while the profile is active: no DNS change to wait for on a switch. All names are renewed at least every 30 days. The certificate covers the main name and all endpoint names (each with *.).
myaddr.z_b_ip_des_hosters: e.g. IP of the hoster or 127.0.0.1
push.direkt: Push messages always go directly over the home line, past the VPN, so that the alarm “All VPNs down” and the reminders arrive at once. The push service sees your home IP; everything else (DDNS, certificate, redirect) stays in the tunnel.
push.ein_feld_leeren_und_speichern: Emptying a field and saving switches the target off. Tokens are never shown; for a new address enter the token again.
push.erinnerung_solange_alle_vpns_ausgef: Reminder while all VPNs are down (minutes)
push.meldungen_bei_einem_wechsel_des: Messages on a VPN profile switch, an outage of all VPNs (with a reminder while it lasts), the recovery, errors of DDNS, certificate, redirect, NPM and Zoraxy, and a renewed certificate. The same message at most once per hour, at most 20 per hour in total.
redirect.lauft_mit_bin_sh_60: Runs with /bin/sh (60 s time limit) and the variables PF_TARGET_URL, PF_TARGET_HOST, PF_PORT, PF_IP, PF_STATUS_CODE, PF_ENTRY_HOST, PF_SSH_KEY, PF_KNOWN_HOSTS and PF_RULES (all rules), PF_HTACCESS and PF_PHP (ready files for all rules). Exit code 0 = ok. Do not print passwords.

redirect.oder_privaten_schlussel_hochlad: or upload a private key (without passphrase)
redirect.offentlichen_schlussel_beim_hos: Add the public key at your hoster (Plesk: Websites & Domains → SSH keys).
redirect.token_mit_der_berechtigung_zone: Token with the permission Zone → Single Redirect → Edit for this zone; for round robin also Zone → Zone → Read, Zone → Workers Routes → Edit and Account → Workers Scripts → Edit. The entry host needs a DNS record with proxy (orange cloud), e.g. AAAA to 100::.
redirect.weiter_myaddr_tools_kann_selbst: (always the current port). myaddr.tools cannot redirect by itself, and the Proton port changes now and then. On every change of exit IP or port the provider runs again.
redirect.weitere_regeln_hint: Each start URL is a section of its own; the first one is the main entry. Every name with the use entry (page Names) gets a section automatically, “Save” takes it over; your own hosts with “Add start URL”. Entry: subdomain (empty = the name itself, * = any subdomain) and one of your entry names or your own host. Target: subdomain (empty = the name itself, * = the same subdomain as the entry) below the chosen target name, port always the current VPN port, always https. “Via” picks the provider. *. entries with a script, with Cloudflare only in round robin.
redirect.neu_aus_namen: new from Names, not saved yet
redirect.weitere_anbieter_hint: Provider 1 sets the main entry. Further providers for other start URLs, e.g. a second Cloudflare account or another web hosting; in each start URL “Via” picks the provider. Several start URLs on the same web hosting belong to the same provider, or one overwrites the other's .htaccess. Each provider runs on its own: if one fails, the others are still updated. All scripts use the same SSH key. In round robin a further Cloudflare provider gets its own Worker.
vpn.1340_standard_passt_auch_wenn: 1340 (default) also works when WireGuard runs nested twice (e.g. a home VPN over the tunnel); a single tunnel needs 1420. If videos or large pages stall, try 1280.
vpn.auf_diese_lan_ip_zeigen: point to this LAN IP. Inbound from the LAN only, nothing is opened to the internet.
vpn.gerate_im_lan_und_im: Devices on the LAN (and in the home VPN) use the same address as from outside, but without the detour through the VPN: portnook also accepts the current port on its own LAN IP and forwards it to the reverse proxy. For this, in your own DNS (e.g. Technitium) let
vpn.mehrere_vpn_zugange_falls_einer: Several VPN accesses in case one fails. The list order is the priority. If the active profile fails, the standby takes over, else portnook starts the next switched-on profile. If all are down, nothing leaves through your home line (kill switch), DDNS reports at most the fallback IP.
vpn.name: Name
vpn.reserve_tunnel: Keep a standby tunnel (the next profile runs all the time)
vpn.reserve_tunnel_hint: The topmost switched-on profile that is not active runs as standby with its own port and its own exit IP. If the active tunnel fails, the standby takes over at once, and the redirect points to its name and port right away. The list order is the priority (1 = most important) and stays fixed; there is no automatic switch back. With Proton it needs a second device slot.
vpn.rotation_hint: Switches to the next switched-on profile below the active one (after the last one back to the first). DNS and rewrite follow at once and are checked afterwards (events).
vpn.rotation_stunden: on outage and every N hours (rotation)
vpn.rotation_uhrzeit: Time (HH:MM, time zone TZ of the container)
vpn.wartezeit_vor_ruckwechsel_minuten: Wait before a new attempt when all profiles are down (minutes)
vpn.wechsel_nach_fehlprufungen_alle_30: Switch after failed checks in a row (every 30 s, after an error every 5 s)
wizard.adresse_deines_reverse_proxys_z: Address of your reverse proxy (e.g. Nginx Proxy Manager or Zoraxy) on your home network. portnook forwards the connections from the Proton port there, TLS ends at the reverse proxy.
wizard.andere_anbieter_z_b_airvpn: other providers (e.g. AirVPN) where you open the port in your customer account; upload the file and enter the ports.
wizard.der_port_wird_per_nat: the port is assigned via NAT-PMP (WireGuard file from the Proton account, with NAT-PMP).
wizard.dns_ipv6_und_skript_eintrage: DNS, IPv6 and script entries (PostUp etc.) are removed for security reasons.
wizard.einen_namen_bei_myaddr_tools: add a name at myaddr.tools (DDNS to the exit IP) and get a Let's Encrypt wildcard certificate.
wizard.mindestens_8_zeichen_das_passwort: At least 8 characters. The password protects the settings of this agent.
wizard.mit_vpn_sieht_dein_internetanbiet: With a VPN your internet provider only sees WireGuard to the VPN provider, and your services are reachable through the VPN's exit IP, without an open port on the router.
wizard.netze_im_heimnetz_die_uber: Networks on your home network that are reached through eth0 instead of the tunnel. Required with Proton: replies to the LAN (also to this WebUI) must not go into wg0.
wizard.notig_mit_vpn_antworten_an: Needed with a VPN: replies to your home network (also to this WebUI and the reverse proxy) must not go into the tunnel, or the connection breaks. Suggested from your IP.
wizard.nur_diese_ports_werden_von: Only these ports are forwarded from wg0 to the reverse proxy. The first one is used for DDNS hints and the redirect host.
redirect.modus_hint: Round robin spreads clients by their IP across the active and the standby tunnel. Works with a script (.htaccess or index.php) and with Cloudflare (portnook then creates a Worker “portnook-redirect”). Each VPN tunnel needs its own connection name (DNS name); if both share one name, everything stays on the active tunnel. If the standby fails, it is taken out of the rotation.
js.rr_no_standby: Round robin: standby not ready, active tunnel only
js.rr_no_name: Round robin: standby has no own connection name, active tunnel only
js.rr_no_port: Round robin: standby has no port yet, active tunnel only
js.rr_off: Round robin: VPN off, fixed port only
pp.intro: Without this option your reverse proxy only ever sees portnook's LAN IP. With it, it gets the visitor's real IP, e.g. for logs, fail2ban or geo blocking.
pp.hilfe: portnook puts a PROXY protocol v2 header in front of every forwarded connection (VPN tunnel, standby and LAN entry). For this portnook accepts the tunnel ports itself instead of forwarding them in the kernel; that needs a bit more CPU. Your reverse proxy must expect the PROXY protocol on its HTTPS port, otherwise every connection fails.
pp.einschalten: Pass the real IP via PROXY protocol
pp.hinweis: Switch your reverse proxy first: Zoraxy under Ingress → Advance Settings → PROXY Protocol, nginx with "listen … proxy_protocol". Nginx Proxy Manager cannot do it yet.
js.pp_bestatigen:
Turn on the PROXY protocol?

Your reverse proxy must expect it on its HTTPS port (Zoraxy: PROXY Protocol on; nginx: listen … proxy_protocol). Otherwise nothing is reachable afterwards. Nginx Proxy Manager cannot do it yet.
